_about: Wording for the FAQ on destination pages (plus areasTitle and areaFrom for the 'area by area' links on country and region pages, and footPopular for the footer's popular destinations), one set per language, read by build.py (destination_faq()). Placeholders: {in} the place mid-sentence, {n} count, {split} the tier list, {checked} month checked, {r}/{names} restaurants, {k} a count, {lo}/{hi}/{mid}/{price} prices, {when} the guide's month, {list}/{m} in 'more'. aNewOne/aUpOne fall back to aNew/aUp. {p} in areaFrom is a price. Optional: and3 (the 'and' before the last of three or more, e.g. English's serial comma). qa…: the "In short" answer beside the title (short_answer(); {name} the place's plain name; languages without qaFirst…/qaAll… split the count with tier…/all…, and use star… for qaStars…). qk…: the Quick answers section (quick_answers(); …H are its headings, {year} the latest stars' year), whose new-stars answer reuses aNew…/aUp…. updated: the "Last updated" line under the figures at the top of each destination page ({date} the day its place file or one of its restaurants last changed, place_day()). srcTitle, srcGuide and srcLine: the 'Sources' line under 'How the prices are counted' ({guide} the MICHELIN Guide link, whose words are srcGuide; {checked} the month prices were checked; {google} and {rates} the ratings and exchange-rate links). nw… and cer…: the 'New Michelin stars' section (new_stars_html(); {when} the guide's month, {date} a day, {onDate} the day as 'on <day>' reads (onDate, onDateVowel: Italian l'8, l'11), {guide} the guide's name, {guideFull} the same in nwGuide (English uses {guide}, the name without 'MICHELIN Guide'), {usual} its translated usual month with any preposition (usualFr 'en mars' in content/ceremonies.json; cerTextNoUsual when there's none), {where} the venue). Optional: nwStar2/3 (a star level when it's not the FAQ's star2/3 form), nwUpOne/nwUpFirstOne (one promotion), nwResultsLink and inEnglish (links to the English-only results and ceremony pages). fullMonths, fullMonth, fullDate and fullDayOne write months and days out in full ({mn} the month's number) for that section. Languages whose month changes in a date add fullMonthsDate (Polish 'marca' where fullMonths has 'marzec'), and an own 'on <day>' form where they have one: fullDateOn with fullMonthsOn (Estonian 'märtsil', Latvian 'martā') or fullDaysOn, the 31 days as they read (Hungarian '16-án', Greek 'την 1η', 'στις 2'). Languages with tricky plurals keep {k} and {when} out of agreement: 'łącznie {k}', '({when})'.
